findings.title: Failure threshold can open an incident before N consecutive failures
findings.body: try_incident_threshold treats a monitor as breached once the most recent check-ins (at most failure_issue_threshold of them) contain no CheckInStatus.OK row. It never requires that window to actually contain failure_issue_threshold check-ins, and every non-OK status, including in-progress, counts as part of the streak. With failure_issue_threshold greater than 1, the first failure on a new monitor, a short history after old check-ins are gone, or a window that still includes in-progress rows will mark the environment ERROR, create a MonitorIncident, and emit issue occurrences. The monitor is then stuck failed even though the configured consecutive-failure count was never reached.

findings.title: Issue context sends raw monitor config, dropping schedule display name
findings.body: get_monitor_environment_context copies the monitor config and, when schedule_type is present, replaces it with get_schedule_type_display() so the occurrence payload has a readable schedule. The dict it returns ignores that copy and puts monitor_environment.monitor.config in the "config" field instead. Issue occurrences therefore still carry the raw schedule type (the integer choice), and the display conversion never reaches Kafka. Consumers of the monitor context will show the wrong schedule type.
